content: Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany has criticized UEFA's Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, claiming they protect elite clubs rather than promoting fairness and preventing teams from going bankrupt. According to Kompany, FFP rules allow established clubs to maintain their advantage and prevent other teams from challenging them, rather than promoting competition and equality. Kompany argues that his club's success is due to the investment of owner Sheikh Mansour, which has brought in more fans and revenue, and that FFP regulations would have made it impossible for City to achieve their current level of success.

Jeff Williams, a 26-year-old England Sevens international, has signed with Aviva Premiership side Bath for next season. Williams, who has scored 36 tries on the World Series circuit and helped England win the Tokyo Sevens, brings a high-tempo style of play and a physical edge to the team. According to Bath head coach Mike Ford and England Sevens head coach Simon Amor, Williams' signing fits the club's policy of recruiting young English talent and suits the team's attacking ethos.

Director David Ayer revealed the first full look at Jared Leto as the Joker in the upcoming movie "Suicide Squad." Leto, who has fully immersed himself in the role, will be the first actor to portray the character on the big screen since Heath Ledger's iconic performance. "Suicide Squad," which also stars Will Smith and Margot Robbie, is set to hit theaters on August 5, 2016.

Three Florida corrections officers, Thomas Jordan Driver, David Elliot Moran, and Charles Thomas Newcomb, have been charged with conspiracy to commit murder in a plot to kill a former inmate who was being released from prison. The men, who were allegedly involved with the Ku Klux Klan, were convinced by a staged fake homicide scene and photographs that the deed had been done, according to court documents. If convicted, they could face up to 30 years in jail each.

A conference call between Manny Pacquiao and the media about his upcoming fight against Floyd Mayweather was abruptly cancelled due to technical difficulties, caused by a large number of calls from boxing writers and broadcasters. Pacquiao was only able to answer one question before the call was cancelled, and the event was supposed to be his last question and answer session before he arrives in Las Vegas next week. The call was scheduled to be rescheduled, and Mayweather is set to address the media in a separate conference call on Wednesday.

Serena Williams achieved a milestone by winning her 700th career match at the Miami Open, which led to a giant celebration cake being presented to her. The world No 1 secured her spot in the semi-finals by defeating Sabine Lisicki in a three-set match, and she will now face Simona Halep for a place in the final. This comes after Andy Murray earlier received a celebratory cake for his 500th career win, as the Miami Open continues to see numerous celebrations for its top players.

Beijing International Airport, also known as Daxing Airport, is building the world's largest terminal to accommodate the significant increase in Chinese tourists traveling worldwide. The new Terminal 1, designed by renowned architect Zaha Hadid, will cover 700,000 square meters and be capable of handling 45 million passengers annually. The terminal's design focuses on creating a sense of openness and space, with flowing lines and a lack of pillars, aiming to provide a welcoming experience for passengers from around the globe.

Manchester United manager Louis van Gaal has confirmed that Wayne Rooney suffered a knee injury during the team's defeat by Everton at Goodison Park. The severity of the injury is still unknown, and Van Gaal stated that it's too early to determine its extent. The injury occurred in the closing stages of the Premier League clash, with Rooney being replaced by Robin van Persie.

Jack Wilshere, an English midfielder, recently went shopping at Waitrose and shared a photo of his overflowing trolley on Instagram, showcasing his staple food requirements. His shopping list included a variety of items such as cereal, eggs, baked beans, and corn on the cob, indicating a focus on protein-rich foods to aid in his recovery from ankle surgery. Wilshere humorously captioned the photo, "This is how my day off was spent....now the worst part, Putting it all away!!!" and asked his followers for help in unloading his groceries.

Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro was hit on the head with a mango by a woman named Marleni Olivo, who had written her name and phone number on the fruit. In response to the incident, Maduro offered Olivo a new apartment as part of the country's housing mission, saying she would receive it within a few days. The unusual incident has gone viral in Venezuela, with Maduro joking about the situation and his critics labeling it a "manguicidio," a play on the words "mango" and "magnicidio."

Carlos Tevez, a former Manchester United and City striker, believes it is harder to score goals in Serie A than the Premier League, attributing this to the stronger defensive presence in Italian football. He criticized Premier League midfields as "non-existent" and stated that defending is better on the continent. Despite his own success in the Premier League, scoring 84 goals and winning three titles, Tevez thinks his current team, Juventus, is more rounded and capable of repeating their Champions League-winning success.

Jamie Carragher has criticized Yaya Toure for allegedly ducking out of the way of Jason Puncheon's free-kick in Manchester City's Premier League loss to Crystal Palace, claiming it was "not acceptable" for a player in his position. Carragher pointed out that the rest of the City wall, including Fernandinho and Vincent Kompany, appeared to be committed to blocking the shot, while Toure seemed hesitant. The incident occurred during a game where City was left nine points adrift of Chelsea, with the defeat coming at a crucial moment in the season.

A 50-year-old Australian man, believed to be from Seymour in Victoria, died suddenly at the 101 Legian Hotel in Kuta, Bali, after collapsing at the Rooftop Restaurant. The man had ordered breakfast and told a waitress that he was not feeling well before suddenly falling to the floor, prompting his friend to call for help. An autopsy is pending to determine the exact cause of death, although a doctor at the scene suspects that the man died of a heart attack.

A private funeral service was held for former Australia cricket captain and commentator Richie Benaud, who died at the age of 84 due to complications from skin cancer. Despite being offered a state funeral by Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott, Benaud's family opted for a smaller, private service attended by close family and friends, as per his wishes. A memorial was later held at the Australian Golf Club, attended by former cricket commentating colleagues, network executives, and Test cricketers past and present, to honor Benaud's legacy as a beloved cricket identity.

Isobel Attwood, a 16-year-old schoolgirl, has been missing for two days after leaving her home in Winchester, Hampshire, on Saturday afternoon. According to friends' social media posts, Isobel is believed to be in Southampton with a man in his 20s, and she has written a message on Facebook stating that she is safe but needs time to get away. Police are becoming concerned for her welfare and are appealing for help to find her, urging her to come home or make contact with them.

Manchester City players, including Sergio Aguero and Yaya Toure, could lose £500,000 each in bonuses if the team fails to qualify for the Champions League this season. The players are on incentivized contracts to help the club stay within financial fairplay requirements, and a top-four finish is crucial for them to receive this payment. Manchester City's chances of qualifying for the Champions League are uncertain, as they currently sit in fourth place and are only four points ahead of Liverpool, who can move into fourth place if they win their remaining matches.

Liverpool defender Martin Skrtel has denied rumors of a potential move away from the club, stating that he will not be leaving Anfield despite his contract expiring in 2016. Skrtel has been linked with Wolfsburg and Napoli, but his agent, Karol Csonto, confirmed that the only offer on the table is a contract extension with Liverpool. Skrtel has made over 200 league appearances for the Reds since arriving in 2008 and is expected to finalize a new contract with the club.

Cheryl Rios, the CEO of Go Ape Marketing in Texas, has faced criticism for her statement that a woman cannot be president due to her "hormones," which she believes would hinder her ability to start a war. Rios initially claimed that her views were based on biblical reasoning, but later clarified that she was referring specifically to the role of President and Commander-in-Chief. Her comments have sparked widespread criticism on social media, with many labeling her a misogynist and hypocrite, despite her assertion that she supports equal rights for women.

Atletico Madrid striker Mario Mandzukic is expected to be fit for the return Champions League quarter-final against Real Madrid at the Bernabeu on Wednesday, despite suffering a cut to the nose and an ankle injury in the first leg. Mandzukic was battered and bruised during the match, with a cut to the nose from an elbow by Sergio Ramos and a punch to the stomach by Dani Carvajal. Coach Diego Simeone has expressed confidence in Mandzukic's fitness, saying he was fine after a training session and will be considered for the starting lineup alongside Antoine Griezmann.

Jose Mourinho had prepared his Chelsea team to deal with Manchester United's Marouane Fellaini by having Kurt Zouma man-mark him, but was initially misled by a hotel doorman who told him Fellaini was not playing. The doorman claimed Fellaini was at the hotel to buy tickets from Eden Hazard, but Mourinho discovered through a Google search that the man in the hotel was actually Fellaini's twin brother Mansour, who bears a resemblance to the United player. In the end, Fellaini did play in Chelsea's 1-0 win over Manchester United, but was successfully dealt with by Kurt Zouma in midfield.

A 45-year-old New Jersey woman, Dawn Milosky, was rescued from her overturned vehicle by police officers in Kinnelon, New Jersey, just as it started to catch fire. Officers Mark Ehrenberg and Ricky Ferriola quickly responded to the scene after a tip-off about erratic driving and managed to free Milosky from her seatbelt and pull her to safety within two minutes. Milosky was then airlifted to Morristown Medical Center, where she is reportedly doing okay, and has been charged with driving while intoxicated and other related offenses.

A farmer in eastern China has gained attention after one of his goats gave birth to a kid with six legs, a rare mutation that has drawn public interest. The baby goat, weighing 5kg at birth, is growing healthily and has an extraordinary appetite, according to its owner, Xiao Qibin. Despite the initial uncertainty about the kid's survival, it has become one of the most playful goats on the farm, with two of its forelegs eventually becoming shorter than the rest.

West Ham is reportedly planning to sign Javier Hernandez, a 26-year-old Mexican striker on loan at Real Madrid from Manchester United, at the end of the season. Hernandez, who scored a late winner in the Champions League quarter-final, will return to Old Trafford and be available for around £7million as he is not in Louis van Gaal's plans. West Ham is part of an extensive summer recruitment programme and is also interested in several other young transfer targets, including Pedro Obiang, Moussa Konate, and Fabian Schar.

Rangers manager Stuart McCall has stated that his future at the club will not be decided before the end of the season, despite his recent revival of the team's fortunes with three successive wins. McCall emphasizes that his side has yet to achieve anything in the Championship and that their focus remains on winning, rather than contract negotiations. He also expressed caution about the potential integration of new signing Shane Ferguson, who is set to arrive at Murray Park next week, due to Ferguson's long-term knee injury.

Werder Bremen secured a 1-0 victory over Hamburg SV, with Franco Di Santo scoring an 84th-minute penalty to keep his team in the running for a Europa League spot. The win moved Werder Bremen up to seventh place in the Bundesliga, while Hamburg SV remained in last place with five matches left in the season. New Hamburg coach Bruno Labbadia suffered a losing return to his bench, with the team facing the possibility of being relegated for the first time in their Bundesliga history.

A two-year-old boy fell into a cheetah exhibit at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo after his parents allegedly dangled him over the edge, causing the child to slip and fall between 10 to 12 feet. Fortunately, the boy was rescued by his parents before firefighters and paramedics arrived, and he was taken to the hospital with minor bumps and bruises. The zoo plans to press child endangerment charges against the family, and the cheetah exhibit was closed following the incident.

Russian TV channel TV Rain gave Hillary Clinton's 2016 presidential campaign video a "mature audiences" rating due to concerns about violating Russia's anti-gay propaganda law, which prohibits public discussion of gay rights near minors. The video features a gay couple holding hands, which led the channel to err on the side of caution to avoid potential repercussions from authorities. This move reflects Russia's controversial law, which has been widely criticized by human rights groups and sparked international protests since its passage in 2013.

Newcastle midfielder Siem de Jong made a comeback from a collapsed lung by playing 45 minutes for the Under 21s against Derby County, but the team lost 2-0. De Jong has struggled with injuries since joining the club last summer, making only one Premier League start and now has an outside chance of featuring in the final six matches of the season. The 26-year-old's return was subdued, and he may not be ready to play in Sunday's match against Spurs, with forgotten striker Facundo Ferreyra replacing him at halftime.

Chef Ally Lees of Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham created a massive three-foot omelette containing 12,000 calories and 945g of protein, which is 16 times the recommended daily amount for a man. The dish, made with 150 fresh eggs, would require a group of at least five people to consume it, according to the chef. Ally Lees said it was the biggest food challenge he has ever taken on, and while he found the omelette "lovely," he didn't think he could eat all of it due to its high protein content.

This summer, Olympic gold medallists Jessica Ennis-Hill, Mo Farah, and Greg Rutherford will appear at the Sainsbury's Anniversary Games in London, a three-day event featuring the world's finest athletes. The event, which includes a two-day Diamond League meeting from July 24-25 and the Sainsbury's IPC Athletics Grand Prix Final on July 26, promises to be one of the biggest events in the summer's sporting calendar. Tickets for the event are now available to the general public, with prices starting from £20 per adult and £12 for concessions on July 24-25, and from £10 on July 26.

In Rio de Janeiro, a snack bar was found to be serving pastries made from the meat of stray dogs, which had been killed with blows to the head. The discovery was made by police investigating claims of slave-like conditions at the eatery, where trafficked Chinese workers were found to be working 18 hours a day without pay. The owner, Chinese Van Ruilonc, admitted to using dog meat in the pastries, which is a traditional Brazilian snack called "pastels," and was reportedly one of a group of Chinese businessmen owning dozens of pastry houses in the city.

Ebony Dickens, a 33-year-old woman from East Point, Georgia, was arrested after posting a threatening message on Facebook under a fake name, "Tiffany Milan." The post, which called for the killing of white police officers, was removed before Dickens' arrest, but law enforcement agencies, including the East Point police, Atlanta police, FBI, and federal Homeland Security Department, were able to identify her and obtain a search warrant for her residence. Dickens was charged with disseminating information related to terrorist acts and was initially held in jail before bonding out with a $10,000 bond.

PSV Eindhoven won the Dutch championship with a 4-1 victory over Heerenveen, securing their first title in seven seasons and putting them out of reach of second-placed Ajax Amsterdam. Striker Luuk de Jong scored two headed goals in the first half, while Memphis Depay added a stunning free kick to put PSV in control. The win marked PSV's 22nd league championship, second only to Ajax's 33 titles in the Netherlands.

An 11-year-old boy named Shiva was allegedly beaten to death by the head teacher, Lalit Verma, of Dwarika Prasad School in Railamau village, India, for stealing another student's pencil and eraser. The incident occurred after the stolen items were discovered in Shiva's bag, and he was subjected to a severe beating, which led to internal bleeding and ultimately his death. Verma has been arrested and charged with culpable homicide not amounting to murder, and an investigation is ongoing to determine the cause of death.

A gastrointestinal illness outbreak has affected 100 people, including 95 passengers and 5 crew members, on the cruise ship Celebrity Infinity. The ship, which departed from San Diego on March 29, is currently being investigated by the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) to determine the cause of the illness. The CDC has sent two staffers to meet the ship in San Diego on Monday, and the cruise line has taken measures such as increased cleaning and disinfection procedures to address the outbreak.

Loren Mathieson's Boston Terrier, Gizmo, has mastered the unique skill of "paw-stand walking," where he walks on his front feet while lifting his back legs vertically in the air. Gizmo performed this trick while trying to get accustomed to new black booties, and the footage has been watched over 80,000 times. The adorable stunt left viewers smiling, with Mathieson laughing as she watched her pet's circus-like trick.

New Orleans has gone smoke-free as of midnight on Tuesday, with a city-wide ban on smoking in most places, including bars, casinos, and restaurants. The unanimous decision by the New Orleans City Council in January aimed to protect the health of workers, such as waiters and musicians, who had to breathe in smoke while doing their jobs. Bar owners and a casino have filed a lawsuit to stop the ban, with fines starting at $50, but none of the city's popular attractions require smoking.

Manchester United secured a hard-earned victory against West Ham United, moving four points clear at the top of the Under 21 Premier League. The match saw a dramatic turnaround, with Josh Harrop scoring twice to level the scores and eventually secure the win, after West Ham initially took a 12-minute lead through Reece Oxford's goal. Harrop's second goal came from a poor handling by the West Ham goalkeeper, allowing him to volley in the effort and seal the victory for Manchester United.

Brisbane's Anglican Archbishop Phillip Aspinall has joined Catholic priest Father Paul Kelly in calling for the removal of Queensland's "gay panic" homicide defence, which reduces a murder charge to manslaughter if the defendant claims their victim made a sexual advance. Archbishop Aspinall supports Father Kelly's calls, stating that violence is never a constructive response to such situations. He also appealed to those who resort to violence and vandalism, emphasizing the need to resist reacting out of fear.

Sandra Bullock has been named the world's most beautiful woman of 2015 by People magazine, joining a long line of actresses who have received the honor. Despite being 50, the oldest woman to receive top honors in the history of the list, Bullock seems to be taking the title in stride, calling it "ridiculous" and emphasizing the importance of inner beauty. The cover story highlights Bullock's home life and her efforts to stay healthy and fit, as well as her happiness with who she is, as she has said she can look in the mirror and like who she sees as long as she's healthy and strong.

At least six people, including four aid workers for the UNICEF agency, were killed in an improvised bomb attack near a U.N. vehicle in the Somali city of Garowe on Monday morning. The terrorist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack, which also resulted in four other workers being seriously injured. Somalia's President, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, condemned the attack, stating that it was not only targeted at the United Nations but also at Somali children, and described it as an attack against the future of the country.

Gary Saurage, a wildlife park owner in Beaumont, Texas, caught a massive 400lb, 11ft-long alligator from a family's backyard pond after it was spotted by a local resident, Art Williams. The alligator, estimated to be around 35 to 40 years old, was safely hauled out of the pond and taken to Saurage's Gator Country wildlife park, where it will join over 400 other alligators. Saurage emphasized the importance of keeping a safe distance from alligators, as they can run at speeds of up to 22 miles per hour on land, and warned against attempting to feed them.

Five militants from the Kurdistan Workers' Party were killed and another was wounded in clashes with Turkish armed forces in the eastern city of Agri, Turkey. Four Turkish soldiers were also wounded in the fighting, which took place ahead of a spring festival, with the Kurdish separatists opening fire from a distance. Turkish leaders, including Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, condemned the attack, with Erdogan describing it as an attempt to intervene in the resolution process with the Kurds.

Two 18-month-old twin boys were pulled from a canal in Yuma, Arizona, after accidentally falling into the water at 9:45 am on Friday. Despite a search effort by police and a U.S. Marine Corps helicopter rescue, the boys were pronounced dead at a Yuma hospital after being flown in for treatment. Detectives investigating the case do not suspect foul play and believe the boys ended up in the canal by accident, with a family member nearby when the incident occurred.

Orlando City, a Major League Soccer (MLS) club, has expressed interest in signing Manchester United's Javier Hernandez, a Mexico international, who has been struggling on loan at Real Madrid. Hernandez would be a significant commercial draw for the Florida-based team, which has a large Latin-American fanbase and is coached by Adrian Heath, a former Everton and Manchester City striker. Eight European clubs, including Southampton, Stoke, and AC Milan, are also interested in signing Hernandez, who is valued at around £8million by Manchester United.

Joel Burger, 24, proposed to his girlfriend Ashley King, 23, and she accepted, paving the way for a Burger-King wedding. The couple has been friends since kindergarten and has been teased about their matching names, which they have now fully embraced. To celebrate their engagement, they posed for photos outside their local Burger King and plan to serve drinks in personalized Burger King cups at their wedding.

A secret 1964 police intelligence report linked a hit band from the 1960s to a notorious paedophile brothel in Battersea, South West London, where Jimmy Savile was also known to frequent. The report, which was uncovered in 2013 during Operation Yewtree, does not specify whether the band and Savile attended the brothel at the same time, but they have been associated with the property. The connection between the band and the brothel was noted, but it was not pursued as a lead for investigation until many years later.

A six-year-old German Shepherd named Sadie from Alberta, Canada, has been filmed playing an electric organ at home, showcasing her musical abilities. In the footage, Sadie switches on the keyboard with her nose, plunks her front paws down on the keys, and produces a minimalist piece with clashing notes. Despite a brief moment of frustration, Sadie confidently performs and even takes a bow after a 20-second rendition, earning praise from viewers who have watched the video over 12,000 times.

A 22-year-old man, Ivan Balashov, was caught for stealing a phone after taking a selfie with the camera of a different phone he was browsing in a shop in Novokuznetsk, Russia. When police were called, they recognized Balashov from the selfie he had taken before stealing the phone, and he was subsequently found guilty and given a three-month suspended sentence. On his way home, Balashov sold the stolen phone in a pawn shop for £120.

A documentary about the life and music of late British singer Amy Winehouse, titled "Amy: The Girl Behind the Name," has released its first trailer ahead of its UK release on July 3. The documentary aims to capture not just Winehouse's artistic talent but also her personal side, featuring unseen footage and previously unheard tracks, and has been endorsed by her family. Winehouse struggled with fame and addiction throughout her career, which was marked by two albums and six Grammys, before her tragic death from alcohol poisoning at the age of 27 in 2011.

This week, several notable TV shows are airing, including "The Big Bang Theory," which features the return of Christine Baranski and Laurie Metcalf as Sheldon and Leonard's mothers, and "Saturday Night Live," hosted by Scarlett Johansson. Other shows airing this week include the season finales of "Mom," "Backstrom," and "Blue Bloods," as well as the season premiere of "Younger," which has been picked up for a second season.

Downton Abbey fans may rejoice as the show's creator, Julian Fellowes, has hinted that some characters from the hit series may return in his new American show, The Gilded Age. The show, set in late 19th Century New York, could feature a young version of Violet, Countess of Grantham, played by Dame Maggie Smith, as well as Robert, the Earl of Grantham, and his American-born wife Cora. Plans for the series have yet to be finalized, but sources at NBC indicate that production may begin soon, with a possible air date as early as next season.

Steven Gerrard is expected to start in the FA Cup semi-final against Aston Villa at Wembley, marking his 36th and potentially final game at the national stadium. Gerrard, who is set to leave Liverpool at the end of the season to join the LA Galaxy, has been out for a month serving a three-match ban but is now back in the side. Manager Brendan Rodgers praised Gerrard, describing him as a "special player" who has consistently produced big goals and moments in big games.

A new, original Dr. Seuss book titled "What Pet Should I Get?" has generated significant interest, with pre-orders continuing to climb and the book's first printing being increased from 500,000 to 1 million copies. The book, which features the siblings from the classic "One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish," is believed to have been written between 1958 and 1962 and was discovered by Dr. Seuss' widow in 2013. The book is set to be released on July 28, marking the first new, original Dr. Seuss book since "Oh, the Places You'll Go!" in 1990.

Jessica Carey surprised her grandmother, Patty Lawing, by revealing a tattoo of a younger Patty on her forearm. The tattoo was based on a childhood portrait of Patty, which Jessica had gotten from her husband, Aaron Carey. Patty's reaction was captured on film, showing her overwhelmed with emotion and shouting "oh my God" upon seeing the tattoo.

Annegret Raunigk, a 65-year-old German primary school teacher, is set to become the oldest woman in the world to give birth to quadruplets, after 18 months of fertility treatment. She has already had 13 children, conceived with five different fathers, and is due to retire this year, but claims she is feeling fit and is not worried about the birth. Raunigk's gynaecologist has mentioned the possibility of an abortion due to the high risk associated with quadruplet pregnancies, but she has decided against this option.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, plans to send an unmanned rover to the moon's surface by 2018, using its Epsilon solid-fuel rocket technology and a SLIM probe, which will help perfect soft-landing technologies for future manned expeditions. The estimated cost of the mission is around ¥10 billion to ¥15 billion ($83.4 million to $125 million), and the lander will use face recognition software to identify craters on the moon's surface. This move could be seen as Japan's attempt to catch up with its Asian neighbors, China and India, which have achieved significant extraterrestrial milestones in recent years, including China's successful lunar rover and India's Mars probe.

A dengue fever outbreak has affected several top Brazilian football clubs, with three players diagnosed with the disease, including Corinthians striker Paolo Guerrero. The players, who will need about two weeks to recover, have been advised to use insect repellent during practice sessions, and clubs have asked health officials to inspect their training centers for mosquito breeding sites. The outbreak has led to players taking precautions such as practicing with protective clothing, and Guerrero has been hospitalized, missing his team's last two games in the Copa Libertadores.

Manchester United striker James Wilson has expressed admiration for his teammates' skills and would like to incorporate one quality from each of them into his own game. Wilson, 19, would take Wayne Rooney's ability to take free-kicks, praising Rooney's daily practice and accuracy on the pitch. He would also like to emulate Robin van Persie's movement and Radamel Falcao's predatory instincts, which he believes would enhance his own game.

A 2-year-old child was struck and killed by a van driven by Archie Brown Jr. in a Milwaukee, Wisconsin residential neighborhood on Sunday evening. Before police arrived, an unidentified gunman shot Brown in the head and a 15-year-old boy, who was not a passenger in the van, also died from gunshot wounds. Police are investigating the incident, with a local alderman suggesting that the shooting may have been carried out in revenge for the child's death.

A teenage boy from Memphis, Tennessee, has gained over 3,000 Twitter followers by posting pictures and videos of himself engaging in "gang life," including posing with guns, cash, and marijuana. The boy's tweets have sparked a backlash from critics who have called his behavior "sad" and "disappointing," with some expressing concern for his well-being and others warning that his actions could lead to negative consequences. Authorities are increasingly aware of the role of social media in perpetuating gang culture, with around 50% of organized gangs in the US maintaining a social media profile.

Former Redgum frontman John Schumann has condemned the use of his song "I Was Only 19" at a Reclaim Australia rally, which aimed to oppose "sharia law, halal tax and Islamisation". Schumann, who wrote the song to promote tolerance and compassion, expressed disappointment that his work was being used to advance ignorance and intolerance. The rallies across Australia erupted into violence, with several arrests reported, including three in Melbourne where over 3,000 people clashed.

Tottenham forward Emmanuel Adebayor has expressed his commitment to the team, rejecting rumors of a potential move away and stating that he is happy to stay and fight for his place. Despite struggling with form and being replaced by homegrown star Harry Kane, Adebayor remains adamant that he will see out the remainder of his contract in north London. The 31-year-old Togo international has made just 16 appearances this season, scoring twice, and his last Premier League goal for Spurs came in October last year.

Former Manchester City player and manager Stuart Pearce believes that manager Manuel Pellegrini deserves more time to turn the club's fortunes around. Pearce thinks that the club should stick with Pellegrini, who has been around long enough to realize that the squad needs significant changes this summer. Pearce also pointed out that the fading influence of Yaya Toure may be a contributing factor to the club's poor run of form, particularly when Toure loses form or is away on international duty.

Hull City manager Steve Bruce remains confident that his team can avoid relegation from the Premier League despite a 2-0 defeat by Southampton, which left them just two points clear of the drop zone. Bruce attributes their struggles to long-term injuries to key players, including Michael Dawson and Nikica Jelavic, who have missed half the season, and Robert Snodgrass, who has been unavailable all season. With six games remaining, including tough fixtures against top teams, Bruce believes that his team can "take a couple of results which will take us over the line" and secure their Premier League status.

A full-scale terror alert was triggered in Reading after a passer-by spotted a dummy wearing a balaclava on a boat with a fake missile launcher on its roof. Thames Valley Police and an Army bomb disposal team responded to the incident, but the reported weapon was found to be purely ornamental. The dummy, complete with a realistic-looking missile and a menacing balaclava, caused panic among locals, with one resident condemning the prank as "not funny at all in this day and age."

Tiger Woods suffered a bizarre injury on the ninth hole at the Masters on Sunday, where he drilled his club into a tree root, causing him to yell in pain. Despite the injury, Woods managed to shake off the pain and complete the competition at 5-under-par, although he claimed to have popped a ligament in his right wrist back into place to do so. Woods ended the round with a score of 73 and tied for 17th place, his best finish in over a year, despite being 13 strokes behind the winner, 21-year-old Jordan Spieth.

Iker Casillas, a 33-year-old Spanish goalkeeper, has expressed his commitment to staying at Real Madrid despite potential competition from David de Gea, who has been linked with a move to his homeland. Casillas, who has spent his entire career at the Bernabeu, claims he will fight for the No. 1 jersey and earn his place on the team rather than leave. He is currently focused on helping Real Madrid defend their Champions League title, which they are hoping to retain by becoming the first team to do so.

A video has surfaced showing a Russian S300 missile launch going horribly wrong, with the rocket barely taking off before plummeting back down to earth, producing a small explosion and a plume of smoke. This incident is likely to be embarrassing for Russian President Vladimir Putin, who has seen a significant increase in the country's defense budget. The footage comes after a previous incident in Ukraine where another rocket launch resulted in the death of six Russian ballistic missile technicians.
